title: Add ablation experiment harness for quantized kernel benchmarks
author: Maya Kwan
description: Motivation: provide a lightweight, reproducible harness for ablation testing of quantized kernels under real inference-like workloads. This PR adds a small experiment runner, README with suggested configs, and adapters that let existing kernel benchmarks use quantized model checkpoints. It is intended for experimentation and does not change production runtime behavior. How to run: 1) pip install -e experiments/quant_bench, 2) export QUANT_CHECKPOINT=/path/to/checkpoint, 3) python experiments/quant_bench/run.py --model rwl-7b --seq-len 1024 --batch 8 --trials 5. The runner supports CPU warmup cycles and optional perf logging to a JSON output (--out results.json). Notes on design: the harness separates workload generation from kernel invocation so we can swap in emulated loads or recorded traffic. It includes hooks for traced runs (OTel) and a small yml config for sweep parameters. Results summary (example): quant int8 kernels reduced memory footprint by ~3.6x at 1.1x median latency for this workload; variance observed across sequence lengths and attention layouts. See experiments/quant_bench/README.md for sample CSV/JSON outputs and plotting scripts. Checklist: add harness + README, add kernel adapter, add quick CI smoke test, basic perf numbers in README. This PR is intended to centralize experimental artifacts and make iterative ablation runs easier for perf researchers. For follow-ups: add a reproducible dataplane recipe and regression dashboards if results look promising.
commits: init: add experiment harness and runner (experiments/quant_bench)
feat: add quantized kernel adapter and interface shim
